note: An epoch link claiming epoch 1. A room's first epoch has no predecessor, so a rung 1 wraps something that is not an earlier epoch's key; the floor of 2 on EpochLink.epoch is what refuses it. (The stronger rule — that a link's epoch must equal the epoch being minted — is a MUST in prose, because a schema cannot compare two of its own members.)

An epoch link with no nonce. Every rung is AEAD ciphertext and a nonce is not optional for one; a link missing it cannot be opened by anybody, and would be stored as a rung that silently severs the chain at that point.

Unknown member inside the link — additionalProperties: false on EpochLink. A rung carries wrapped key material and nothing descriptive; an extra member is the obvious place to leak what the sealing exists to hide.

Minting epoch 1. An epoch advances by exactly one from an existing room, whose first epoch is 1 already; a request to mint it is either a re-registration or an off-by-one, and both would reset a room rather than advance it.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
